title: The Trail of the Upper Fly River
premise: Orsen Quintana, a salvage diver haunted by the drowning of her brother, is hired to recover a chest from a wreck in the Upper Fly River — a chest bearing the seal of a nation that no longer exists. Inside are documents proving a wartime atrocity that three governments will kill to bury, and a map to the river's forbidden source where the rest of the archive lies hidden. Pursued by a naval officer who was once her lover, Orsen travels upstream through gorges, mission stations, and drowned villages, learning that stopping anywhere costs someone their life. At the source she must choose between destroying the evidence to save the people who sheltered her or carrying it out to honor her brother's memory; she sends it downstream hidden in a rival salvager's hull, burns the map, and finally lets herself stop moving.
about_author: Juniper Fairweather is the pen name of a former river-boat deckhand who spent six seasons on the waterways of Papua New Guinea before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people whose pasts travel with them like ballast.

chapters.title: The Wreck Nobody Names
chapters.summary: Orsen dives a navy-cordoned wreck in the Fly River delta, recovering salvage while dodging patrol boats, and finds a brass fitting stamped with an unfamiliar national seal. Her POV establishes her restless competence and grief for her brother Tomas, lost diving years ago. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpened by curiosity.

chapters.title: Chest of a Dead Flag
chapters.summary: Still Orsen's POV: she raises a sealed iron chest from the silt, and that night a stranger named Ila Mero offers triple its weight in gold for it sight unseen. Orsen opens it instead, finding documents in a dead language and a wax-sealed map. Beat: greed gives way to dread.

chapters.title: The Officer on the Pier
chapters.summary: Naval Lieutenant Dario Voss — Orsen's former lover — arrives asking questions about the chest, all courtesy and threat. His POV reveals he is under orders to retrieve it quietly and that his superiors fear what's inside. Beat: old love curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: What Tomas Knew
chapters.summary: Orsen deciphers enough to learn her brother had dived this same wreck months before his death, and that his last letter matches phrases in the documents. She realizes his drowning may not have been an accident. Beat: grief re-forged into purpose.

chapters.title: Upstream at Night
chapters.summary: Orsen slips away aboard Ila's shallow-draft barge as Voss's launch searches the delta. First-person tension of running rapids in darkness, leaving behind the only life she could tolerate. Beat: escape that feels like exile.

chapters.title: The Drowned Village
chapters.summary: The barge passes a village flooded by a dam project; survivors living on stilts recognize the dead nation's seal and beg Orsen to burn the papers. Her POV shows the human cost of the secret she carries. Beat: guilt taking root.

chapters.title: Ila's Price
chapters.summary: Ila Mero's POV: he confesses he sold information about the wreck once already, and that men died for it. He warns Orsen that everyone who helps her becomes a target, then chooses to keep going anyway. Beat: complicity and loyalty entwined.

chapters.title: Gorge of Whispers
chapters.summary: Voss's POV: his patrol boat corners them in a narrow gorge, but he hesitates when he sees Orsen at the rail, letting the barge slip through a fog bank. Flashbacks to their shared past. Beat: duty cracking against love.

chapters.title: The Mission at Kiunga Bend
chapters.summary: Aging missionary Sister Anselm shelters them and translates part of the documents: records of a massacre covered up at war's end, witnessed by men still alive upstream. Beat: the abstract crime acquires faces and names.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Confluence
chapters.summary: Mercenaries hired by a mining consortium attack the barge; Ila is wounded covering Orsen's retreat into the jungle. Her POV, breathless action and first real blood spilled on her account. Beat: survival begins costing others.

chapters.title: Leech Country
chapters.summary: Orsen drags wounded Ila through swampland toward the highlands, hallucinating from fever, sustained by memories of Tomas teaching her to swim. Beat: endurance stripped to its essentials; memory as lifeline.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Daughter
chapters.summary: In a highland hamlet, an old woman recognizes the map — her father drew it hiding the archive at the river's source. She gives Orsen the final route but refuses to come, saying some debts are paid by staying. Beat: inheritance of witness.

chapters.title: Voss Closes In
chapters.summary: Voss's POV: ordered to use lethal force now, he falsifies his position reports to buy Orsen time, knowing it ends his career. He radios one warning: 'They're coming by air.' Beat: love choosing treason.

chapters.title: The Airstrip Ambush
chapters.summary: Consortium helicopters strafe the hamlet; Orsen helps evacuate villagers, and Sister Anselm is killed protecting the documents' copies. Orsen's POV, fury and helplessness. Beat: the price of survival made undeniable.

chapters.title: Source of the Fly
chapters.summary: Orsen climbs alone into the misted headwaters and finds the cave archive: crates of testimony, photographs, names. Among them, Tomas's own signed statement — he had found the truth first. Beat: awe collapsing into devastation.

chapters.title: The Choice at the Cave Mouth
chapters.summary: Voss arrives unarmed, having abandoned his command. He argues the evidence will be buried anyway and the witnesses slaughtered; Orsen argues silence buries Tomas twice. They are interrupted by the mercenaries' arrival. Beat: love against duty fully joined.

chapters.title: Fire on the Water
chapters.summary: Climax: Orsen and Voss fight off the mercenary team at the cave, using the terrain and a rigged fuel drum; Ila, recovered, arrives with highland allies to turn the tide. Voss takes a bullet meant for Orsen. Beat: sacrifice answering sacrifice.

chapters.title: Downstream in a Rival's Hull
chapters.summary: Dying plan: Orsen hides the archive inside a consortium salvage vessel's double hull, trusting the current and the enemy's own greed to carry the truth to port and press attention. Beat: cunning over force; letting go of control.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Orsen burns the map and the duplicates, keeping only Tomas's statement to read once and release to his name. Quiet chapter, her POV, mourning Voss who survives but is court-martialed and disappears into custody. Beat: grief given ceremony.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Weeks later the archive surfaces in foreign newspapers; hearings begin; the consortium fractures. Orsen watches from a delta tavern, unnamed in every report, as Ila laughs beside her. Beat: justice arriving sideways, unowned.

chapters.title: Anchored
chapters.summary: Orsen buys a small boat and moors it — deliberately, permanently — at the drowned village, helping rebuild stilt houses. For the first time she unpacks everything she owns. Beat: stillness chosen, not imposed.

chapters.title: The Trail Ends Where It Began
chapters.summary: Final chapter: a letter reaches her from Voss, alive under a new name, asking nothing. Orsen reads it on her porch above the river, folds it away, and dives into clean water — swimming, at last, for no one but herself. Beat: memory honored, movement ended, love released.
